device.description: quad 16-bit voltage-output DAC with internal reference, 24-bit serial interface, quick load, daisy-chain SDO, double-buffered inputs (LOAD, LDAC) and reset to zero or mid scale
device.note: dac7654.pdf (SBAS263A) p.1 (features: power-on reset, description), p.3-4 (electrical characteristics: IOVDD 2.7-5.25 V, VDD/VCC 4.75-5.25 V, VIH 0.7 IOVDD), p.5 (pin assignments), p.6 (terminal functions), p.19 (theory of operation: 24-bit word), p.22 (digital interface, Table 1 truth table), p.23 (24-bit word, quick load, Table 2 shift register, Table 3 data word, 3 V to 5 V logic interface), p.24 (serial data output, daisy chain, coding), p.25 (Figure 58), p.26 (Table 4 timing)

registers.name: SR
registers.note: internal: the 24-bit serial shift register (A1 A0 QUICK LOAD, five unused bits, D15-D0), shifted out on SDO

commands.name: Write
commands.note: 24-bit word A1 A0 QUICK-LOAD X X X X X D15-D0, MSB first, clocked on CLK rising (Table 3, Figure 58). Quick load 1: the code goes to all four input registers; 0: to the one A1 A0 select (channelMap on the 3-bit A1 A0 QL capture). The shift register goes to the input register(s) while LOAD is low; modeled as written when CS rises. The last 24 bits before CS rises are decoded

protocol.note: SDO is the shift register's output (driven, p.24); CS and CLK are ORed, CS should rise only while CLK is high (p.23), hence mode 3

ldac.note: DAC register load, rising-edge triggered: all DAC registers (p.6, Table 1)

clear.note: rising-edge triggered: loads zero (RSTSEL low) or mid scale 8000h (RSTSEL high)

notModeled: analog: outputs, force/sense pins, offset range pins (unipolar/bipolar), internal references, single/dual supply operation, glitch suppression track-and-hold, settling

LOAD: the shift register is copied into the addressed (or, with quick load, every) input register while LOAD is low; the schema has no load-strobe pin, so the word is written when CS rises (a frame without a LOAD pulse still updates the input register in the model)
RST does not change the serial shift register in the chip (the model's clear leaves SR as well)
power-on reset: the features list a power-on reset but no power-on code is given (reset 0)
daisy chain: SDO shifts the previous 24-bit word, then the real part passes the incoming bits through; the model shifts the previous word then zeros, so chained devices do not receive data
CS and CLK are interchangeable (ORed); a CS rising edge while CLK is low shifts one extra bit
VDD must be 5 V (internal logic) while IOVDD sets the 2.7-5.25 V interface levels; vcc is the IOVDD range
timing limits of Table 4 (no SDO propagation delay is given)
variants: DAC7654YCT is the only orderable part in the skeleton. DAC7634 (dac7634.pdf) uses the same 24-bit word with external references in an SSOP-48; DAC7664 is the parallel-interface sibling.
